## Definition references

[[lem-budgeted-verifier-generation-termination-and-calls]]: proves termination, the output rules, and the finite draw, evaluation and comparison bounds under the supplied-call model.

The prompt weights are uniform. Response draws, reward and policy-mass evaluations, scalar arithmetic, square roots, logarithms and comparisons are supplied terminating exact operations with finite per-call costs. Draws return supported responses with the specified independent law. Also supply an exact total domain oracle $M_U:\mathbb R^d\to\{0,1\}$, returning $1$ exactly on $U$, and an exact objective-gradient oracle: given the frozen outer-iteration data and a parameter in $U$, it returns the Euclidean gradient of $F_t$ when that total derivative exists and returns undefined-gradient otherwise. Both oracles terminate on every call with finite per-call cost. The gradient oracle includes the fixed finite objective data and any policy evaluations needed for its decision. This is a supplied-oracle model; it asserts neither an algorithm for deciding differentiability of arbitrary functions nor a general membership algorithm for arbitrary open sets.
